input.rationale: Requested execution of the three-order probe, which adds the discriminating delivery order in which the command-carrying reply is adopted last before the quorum trigger. Local feedback on the added order keeps the owner's command while the two orders recorded by the previous receipt lose it, so the receipt for this revision should show the adopted value following the order rather than the reply set.

scope.description: Owner replica 0 proposes X on its own instance (0,0), replica 1's non-equal pre-accept reply is delivered and replica 1 then fails, so the owner enters the Accept phase at ballot 0 towards replicas 2 and 3; replica 3 accepts without ever pre-accepting (its state holds no command), and the owner's AcceptReplies are left in flight. The owner, alive and still holding X, then runs startRecoveryForInstance(0,0); the harness delivers the Prepare replies of replicas 2, 3 and 4 in a chosen order (replica 2 carries X at value ballot 0, replicas 3 and 4 carry no command at the same ballot) and records whether the owner re-proposes a command and what its instance holds afterwards. The test runs the same message set twice with the empty reply last in one run and first in the other. The order parameter is now applied: run A delivers the replies in the order 2,4,3, run B in the order 3,4,2 and run C in the order 3,2,4, and each run records the order actually delivered.
assumptions: Same construction, transport boundary and crash model as the other experiments in this harness.
Delivery order among the prepare replies is chosen by the harness, which is what a real network does not fix; the read order is not altered.
No production logic is modified.
The number of delivered prepare replies (self plus three peers) means the quorum trigger fires at the second peer reply, which is what the two orders are meant to probe.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop.

experiment.prefix: The harness drives the owner's proposal and accept phase through the target's own handlers, fails replica 1 after its reply, delivers the Accept to replicas 2 and 3, then calls the owner's startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) and delivers each collected PrepareReply to the owner, recording the owner's leader-bookkeeping state (status, appended count, nacks, prepared flag) and the instance's command length before and after the dispatch. Each recipient's messages are collected before delivery and then delivered in the order declared for that run, with the delivered order recorded.
experiment.requirement: A recovery of an instance must not drop the instance's command when a reply without a command arrives at the same value ballot as replies that carry one, and the adopted value must not depend on the delivery order of equally admissible replies.
experiment.responsibility: The recovering replica's own adoption loop and dispatch (epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246 and 1291-1313): the replies are the acceptors' honest answers at their stored ballots.

comparisons.description: Run A (replies 2,4,3): the instance still holds the owner's command after the recovery; violated when an empty command is adopted instead.

Run B (replies 3,4,2): with the command-carrying reply arriving last among the delivered set, the instance still holds the owner's command; a violated outcome here shows the adopted value is fixed by the replies present when the quorum trigger fires rather than by the full set.

Run C (replies 3,2,4): the command-carrying reply is the second delivered, so it is the last adopted before the quorum trigger; the instance is expected to keep the owner's command here, which would show the outcome is fixed by which reply is adopted last before the trigger rather than by the reply set.

experiment.revision_reason: Added a third delivery order, 3,2,4, in which the command-carrying reply is the second one delivered and therefore the last adopted before the quorum trigger. This is the discriminating case: the first two orders put an empty reply in that position, while this one puts the command-carrying reply there. Scenario, handlers and compared fields are unchanged.

scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) constructed in-process with the package's own field and RPC-table initialization, without peer sockets and without the run() loop, so handler execution is deterministic. All inter-replica traffic is the package's own marshaled RPC structs: each bcast runs SendMsg into a captured byte buffer and every delivery decodes a fresh object from those bytes, preserving the transport serialization boundary; delivery is FIFO per link and messages to a crashed replica are dropped. The executed scenario is: replica 1 pre-accepts a conflicting command on its own instance (2,0); leader replica 0 proposes X (PUT key 1) on instance (0,0); replica 1 replies non-equal then crashes; replica 0 runs the Accept phase at ballot 0 to replicas 2 and 3; replica 0 crashes after the Accept broadcast and before consuming any AcceptReply; replica 3 (which received only the Accept, holds no command, and has crtInstance[0] == 0) calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) as its own executor would after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD; the quiescent message exchange is then completed.
assumptions: Replica construction mirrors epaxos.New minus peer connections, the run() loop and ComputeClosestPeers, so PreferredPeerOrder is the constructor order (id+1+i) mod N.
InstanceSpace rows hold 32 entries instead of MAX_INSTANCE (10M); only instances 0..2 are used, so no code path indexes beyond the allocated row.

The auxiliary broadcast of replica 1's conflicting proposal is discarded; only its local conflict state (conflicts[2][key 1]) is used as the premise that makes the leader's pre-accept reply non-equal and therefore forces the Accept phase.

Crashes are modelled as: the replica stops consuming messages, no further message is delivered to it, and every other replica's Alive flag for it is cleared, matching the target's mechanism for deciding broadcast recipients.
Replica 3's recovery is invoked through startRecoveryForInstance, the same function the target's executor invokes from instancesToRecover after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD.
excluded: No client connection path, no execution of the state machine, no recovery timer loop, and no master/BeTheLeader designation (IsLeader stays false, as epaxos.New sets it).

comparisons.description: The command the recovery proposes for instance (0,0) equals the PUT carried by the prepare reply with the highest value ballot (the quorum-held value X); violated when the recovered PreAccept carries the NOOP (cmd_op 0) although quorum_reply_command_op is 1.

A replica that held X after the Accept phase still holds X once the recovered proposal has run to quiescence; violated when the live holder ends up with the NOOP (cmd_op 0) because the recovered PreAccept overwrote its command.

scope.description: Variant of the value-adoption harness that first lets the instance owner commit the value X and then fail, so that the same instance is recovered by a replica that holds no command while another live replica holds X committed. scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) constructed in-process with the package's own field and RPC-table initialization, without peer sockets and without the run() loop, so handler execution is deterministic. All inter-replica traffic is the package's own marshaled RPC structs: each bcast runs SendMsg into a captured byte buffer and every delivery decodes a fresh object from those bytes, preserving the transport serialization boundary; delivery is FIFO per link and messages to a crashed replica are dropped. The executed scenario is: replica 1 pre-accepts a conflicting command on its own instance (2,0); leader replica 0 proposes X (PUT key 1) on instance (0,0); replica 1 replies non-equal then crashes; replica 0 runs the Accept phase at ballot 0 to replicas 2 and 3; replica 0 crashes after the Accept broadcast and before consuming any AcceptReply; replica 3 (which received only the Accept, holds no command, and has crtInstance[0] == 0) calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) as its own executor would after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD; the quiescent message exchange is then completed.
assumptions: Replica construction mirrors epaxos.New minus peer connections, the run() loop and ComputeClosestPeers, so PreferredPeerOrder is the constructor order (id+1+i) mod N.

scope.description: Five replicas (F=2) in the existing harness. Owner replica 0 proposes command X with a real defs.GPropose attached (command id 77, reply writer over a local buffer); replica 1 holds a conflicting command so its pre-accept reply is non-equal, and replica 1 fails after replying; replica 3, which holds no command, recovers instance (0,0) while the owner is still alive; the quiescent exchange is completed; the owner's propose channel is then drained and its instance state, pending proposals and reply writer size are recorded. After the replacement decision and the observed re-queue, the harness calls handlePropose with the re-queued proposal (creating instance (0,1)), delivers that instance's pre-accept replies, and invokes the package's own execution entry point for it, recording the execution result, the reply writer size and the decoded reply.
assumptions: Same construction, transport boundary and crash model as the other experiments in this harness.
The owner stays alive throughout, modelling a slow but reachable owner whose instance is decided by another replica's recovery.
No executor goroutine runs, so any reply observed would have to come from the recovery/handleCommit paths rather than from the state-machine execution path.
The execution entry point is invoked directly, as the package's executeCommands goroutine would, because the harness runs no run() loop.
excluded: No run() loop, no executeCommands goroutine and no client socket; the client request is supplied as the target's own defs.GPropose value.

scope.description: Same 5-replica harness as the recovery-ballot experiment. Owner replica 0 proposes X on instance (0,0) and enters the Accept phase at ballot 0 towards replicas 2 and 3 (replica 1's non-equal reply is delivered first and replica 1 then fails); replica 0's AcceptReplies are left in flight; replica 2 then recovers the instance at its own ballot 7, so the accepting peers store bal 7, and replica 2 fails after broadcasting that Prepare. Two further recovery attempts are then made at replica 1 and replica 3, whose fixed ballots for a non-owned instance are 6 and 8 respectively, and each attempt's Prepare/PrepareReply traffic and follow-up messages are recorded.
assumptions: Same construction, transport boundary and crash model as the value-adoption and recovery-ballot experiments; in-process replicas, marshaled RPC structs decoded per delivery, FIFO per link, no delivery to crashed replicas.

excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop in the harness.

basis.prefix: The harness drives the owner's proposal and accept phase through the target's own path, delivers replica 2's higher-ballot Prepare so the peers store bal 7 and then fails replica 2, and finally calls startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) first at replica 1 and then at replica 3, delivering each attempt's Prepare/PrepareReply traffic through handlePrepare/handlePrepareReply and recording tried, matching and follow-up messages.

basis.responsibility: The target's own ballot policy (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451 makeBallot) and its rejection handling (epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1235 handlePrepareReply): the peers answer honestly with the ballot they stored and the recoverers are ordinary replicas.
